1.explanation: All four of these files define and consume only the camel-cased `ariaLabel` prop (or only the kebab-cased `ariaLabel` without accepting the alternate syntax) and then render it as `aria-label` on the DOM element. To follow React and WAI-ARIA guidelines, they need to be refactored to accept both `['aria-label']` and the deprecated `ariaLabel` (via deprecate()) in their prop destructuring and propTypes, normalize them internally, and then forward `aria-label` to the rendered element. This will give the developer consistency across all components and maintain backward compatibility.
1.bug_scenario: In the Carbon React storybook for Modal (v1.17.0), the <Modal> component correctly accepts an `aria-label` prop (hyphen-case) to provide an accessible label for screen readers. However, in most other React components (e.g. ComboBox) the prop is defined as the camel-cased `ariaLabel` instead of `aria-label`. This inconsistency means some components support only one of the two prop names, breaking the JSX convention that ARIA attributes in React should remain kebab-case. The repro shows Modal using `aria-label="Add a custom domain"`, but ComboBox only accepts `ariaLabel="Choose an item"`, leading to inconsistency and accessibility tooling flags.
